summary: The study investigates the self-limiting growth mechanism in chloride atomic layer epitaxy (ALE) using GaCI as a precursor. The adsorption and desorption processes of GaCI on GaAs substrates were analyzed using temperature programmed desorption (TPD) and surface photo-absorption (SPA) methods. The results indicate that GaCI adsorbs strongly on Ga-terminated surfaces with an adsorption energy of 32 kcal mol-1 and on As-terminated surfaces with 38 kcal mol-1. The presence of H2 is crucial for the reaction of GaCI with hydrogen, leading to the release of Cl as HC1 and the formation of Ga atoms. The short residence time of GaCI on the Ga-terminated surface (~10-3 s at 450 °C) contributes to the self-limiting growth mechanism.
evidence: The growth process of chloride atomic layer epitaxy (ALE) using GaCI is studied using the temperature programmed desorption method (TPD), the surface photo-absorption (SPA) method and ab initio molecular orbital calculations. From the TPD measurements, the GaCI adsorption energy is calculated to be 32 kcal mol-1 and 38 kcal mol-1 for Ga-terminated and As-terminated surfaces respectively. In the absence of H2, the Ga-CI bond appears to be very stable in the adsorption state. Process simulation using a simple cluster model of (AsH2)2-GaCI indicates that adsorption is completed by forming tr and ~ covalent bonds, and that there is hardly any self-dissociation of the Ga-CI bond. From SPA measurements in the ALE system with ambient H2, a strong similarity is found between the spectra of the GaCl-supplying surface and the Ga-covered surface. Based on these results, a model of the chemical process in chloride ALE is proposed where adsorbed GaCI molecules can react immediately with hydrogen and CI is released from the surface as HC1. A self-limiting mechanism results from the very short residence time of GaCI (~ 10-3s at 450 °C) on the Ga-terminated surface.
